### 68be77639 — .claude/skill-observations/log.md

```diff
@@ -4103,0 +4104,14 @@
+ ### Observation 866: A "nothing happened" check that reads a value which is never set passes whatever the app does   «chat kept»
+    «chat kept»
+ **Status:** OPEN   «chat kept»
+ **Date:** 2026-11-08   «chat kept»
+ **Session context:** chat 5, `claude/pr-oil-earn-ffbf07` — OIL Earn on the Scheduler Board (D1783: a tap on a puck that cannot earn picks nothing). Numbered past 865, the highest on the other branches.   «chat kept»
+ **Skill:** New skill candidate: none — the walk-script and drawing-check method (`raptor-port/docs/walk-scripts.md`, `raptor-port/scripts/drawcheck/`), and the bug-check order's §8 (tests find rather than confirm)   «chat kept»
+ **Type:** open-source   «chat kept»
+ **Phase/Area:** writing an assertion that something did NOT happen (nobody picked, no window opened)   «chat kept»
+    «chat kept»
+ **Issue:** Two checks in one job proved "nothing happened" by reading something that never changes. (1) The drawing check's "the tap picked nobody" step read `window.SELID`, a name that does not exist in the built app; it was always undefined, so the step passed even on the build where the tap visibly picked the man blue. The same name had been written into the walkers' brief. (2) Two unit tests proved "the ALL AVAIL window opened" by finding its frame on the page; the frame is always there, hidden, so "opened" was always true. Both were found only because a reproduction on screen disagreed with a green check. They were fixed by reading the mark the app draws (`.puck.sel` on the board) and the frame's shown state (`.availwin:not([hidden])`).   «chat kept»
+ **Suggested improvement:** In `walk-scripts.md`'s rules for a step's assertion, and in the bug-check order §8: every assertion of absence ("nothing picked", "no note", "not opened") is first run once against a state where the thing DID happen (a positive control: tap an ordinary puck and see the same read report it picked), and the step names that control. A read of a global, a frame or an attribute that never changes value across the two states fails the step.   «chat kept»
+ **Principle:** A check that something did not happen is only evidence if the same check, run where it did happen, says so; run the positive case once before trusting the negative.   «chat kept»

The same name had been written into the walkers' brief. (2) Two unit tests proved "the ALL AVAIL window opened" by finding its frame on the page; the frame is always there, hidden, so "opened" was always true. A read of a global, a frame or an attribute that never changes value across the two states fails the step.   «step kept»

+ **Suggested improvement:** in the skill's RED section, a short case: "code written before the test" — reverse-apply the fix's own diff to get the old behaviour, assert the file changed, run red, restore under a trap, run green, in one run of the shared resource."   «chat kept»
+ **Principle:** when the fix came first, recreate the old behaviour by taking back only the fix's own diff — never by checking out an older file — prove the take-back happened, and restore it by a trap, so the red run costs no second turn of a shared resource and cannot leave the old code behind.   «chat kept»

- **Issue:** A new browser test asserted that a short label ("No document") ends inside a fixed-width table column, with a 0.5px tolerance. It was written, proved red-then-green and pushed on a Windows PC only. On the CI's Linux machines, whose fallback sans-serif is much wider, the label overflowed the column by 3px at every width, so the test failed at all five widths and the merge stalled until the next chat diagnosed it. The same trap was met and documented on 23 Oct 26 (Observation 680, now ACTIONED: the gates guide says to rerun with wider letters forced from the first paint), and the repo already had a pattern for it — two tests pin Arial / Liberation Sans so a fit is measured in letters close to the owner's devices on every machine. The documented step was not taken, because nothing in the act of writing such a test calls for it.   «step kept»
- **Suggested improvement:** Make it a default rather than a judgement: in the bug-check order §8 (writing the tests) and the gates guide's trap, "a new browser test that asserts text fits a fixed width pins its letters from the first paint (Arial, Liberation Sans) unless the test is about the device's own letters; and before its first push it is run once with wide letters (Verdana) in that place, where it must fail only if the layout itself is too tight." A cheaper guard still: a unit check over `e2e/*.spec.ts` that flags a new `getBoundingClientRect` text-width assertion in a test with no pinned font — filed for the next review to weigh.   «step kept»
- **Principle:** When a system draws text in whatever font each machine has, every assertion about text width is an assertion about one machine's font. Pin the font the assertion is about, from the first paint, and prove the test both ways (fails on the old layout, passes on the new) in that font — otherwise the first other machine finds the gap.   «step kept»

Pooling every run's raw intervals into buckets (under 20, one refresh skipped, 34.5–50, over 50) showed a fivefold rise in skipped refreshes; a second run with only the suspect style switched off (injected CSS) showed the cost was that one rule, and three cheaper variants were ruled out in minutes. One run's "the page works a third less" did not repeat.   «step kept»
-    «step kept»
- **Suggested improvement:** A frame measure records every raw interval, reports buckets around each refresh multiple rather than one threshold count, repeats the run before believing a total, and diagnoses by switching the suspect rule off for one run before any fix is written.   «step kept»
-    «step kept»
- **Principle:** A threshold placed on a quantised value measures rounding; bucket around the quanta, repeat the run, and isolate a suspected cause by removing it alone.   «step kept»

- ### Observation 887: A pull request that clashes with main starts no checks, and nothing says so   «step kept»
-    «step kept»
- **Status:** OPEN   «step kept»
- **Date:** 2026-11-08   «step kept»
- **Session context:** Chat 13, the schedule's marks and words (pull request 691); numbered past 886, the highest on another open branch.   «step kept»
- **Skill:** New skill candidate: shipping-checks (the rule lives in `.claude/rules/shipping.md` §The checks)   «step kept»
- **Type:** open-source   «step kept»
- **Phase/Area:** after a push — waiting for the pull request's run   «step kept»
-    «step kept»
- **Issue:** Two pushes to an open pull request started no GitHub Actions run — only the preview host's checks appeared. The cause, found only after both: notes-only pull requests merged into `main` meanwhile had made the branch clash (its merge state "CONFLICTING / DIRTY"), and GitHub does not start `pull_request` workflows on a pull request it cannot merge. The same day another chat met it twice ("the pull request had gone into a clash, so its run never started"). Each time the agent first waited for a run that was never coming.   «step kept»
- **Suggested improvement:** In `shipping.md` §The checks, beside "read the run list before a push": right after any push to an open pull request, read its merge state (`gh pr view <n> --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus`); CONFLICTING means no run will start — bring `main` in first. Better, a guard: the push hook prints the merge state after the push and says so when it is CONFLICTING.   «step kept»
- **Principle:** When a check is expected to start by itself, confirm it started; a missing run is a signal, and the most common silent cause is that the platform refused to build the merge.   «step kept»
-    «step kept»
- ### Observation 888: A blind reader that compacts gets the host's handoff pasted in by the start hook   «step kept»
-    «step kept»

-    «step kept»
- **Issue:** The fresh, blind Opus reader ran long enough to compact. The project's compaction start hook then pasted the branch's HANDOFF.md block into it — the host's own record of the walk's fault and its fix, which the reader was meant not to see. The reader said so in its report, so its read was not fully blind (noted in the evidence sheet). Related: Observations 842 (what a start hook injects) and 852 (a blind reader's findings leaking).   «step kept»
- **Suggested improvement:** The compaction start hook pastes the HANDOFF block only into the chat that owns the branch — not into a helper or reader session (tell them apart by the session's parent or a marker the reader's brief sets); until then, every blind reader's brief says "if a pasted handoff block appears after a compaction, do not read it, and say so in the report", and the host sizes a read to finish before the reader would compact.   «step kept»
- **Principle:** Anything injected into a session automatically can break a reader's blindness; blindness must be guarded where the injection happens, not only in the brief.   «step kept»

- **Issue:** Two pushes to an open pull request started no GitHub Actions run — only the preview host's checks appeared. The cause, found only after both: notes-only pull requests merged into `main` meanwhile had made the branch clash (its merge state "CONFLICTING / DIRTY"), and GitHub does not start `pull_request` workflows on a pull request it cannot merge. The same day another chat met it twice ("the pull request had gone into a clash, so its run never started"). Each time the agent first waited for a run that was never coming.   «step kept»
- **Suggested improvement:** In `shipping.md` §The checks, beside "read the run list before a push": right after any push to an open pull request, read its merge state (`gh pr view <n> --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus`); CONFLICTING means no run will start — bring `main` in first. Better, a guard: the push hook prints the merge state after the push and says so when it is CONFLICTING.   «step kept»
- **Principle:** When a check is expected to start by itself, confirm it started; a missing run is a signal, and the most common silent cause is that the platform refused to build the merge.   «step kept»

-    «step kept»
- **Issue:** The fresh, blind Opus reader ran long enough to compact. The project's compaction start hook then pasted the branch's HANDOFF.md block into it — the host's own record of the walk's fault and its fix, which the reader was meant not to see. The reader said so in its report, so its read was not fully blind (noted in the evidence sheet). Related: Observations 842 (what a start hook injects) and 852 (a blind reader's findings leaking).   «step kept»
- **Suggested improvement:** The compaction start hook pastes the HANDOFF block only into the chat that owns the branch — not into a helper or reader session (tell them apart by the session's parent or a marker the reader's brief sets); until then, every blind reader's brief says "if a pasted handoff block appears after a compaction, do not read it, and say so in the report", and the host sizes a read to finish before the reader would compact.   «step kept»
- **Principle:** Anything injected into a session automatically can break a reader's blindness; blindness must be guarded where the injection happens, not only in the brief.   «step kept»

- **Issue:** A filed note's advice for commands that wait on input was "give every script `< /dev/null`". Measured before building: right for `cat` and `node`, but Python on Windows takes `/dev/null` for a keyboard (`isatty()` True) and opens its interactive prompt, which loops until stopped — the measuring itself hung two minutes on it. Second: the hook settings file is read when a chat starts, so a hook added mid-chat does not run in that chat; a "proof live" there shows nothing.   «step kept»
- **Suggested improvement:** In the hook-writing conditions: measure each remedy a note proposes, per tool and interpreter, before a refusal message repeats it; prove a new hook by running the settings file's exact command on a refused and an allowed input (stdin JSON), and leave the in-chat proof to the next new chat, saying so in the handoff.   «step kept»
- **Principle:** A workaround recorded once is a claim like any other; measure the cure as well as the fault, in each environment the advice will reach.   «step kept»

-    «step kept»
- **Issue:** A one-off picture script written to the session's scratch folder failed at once with "module not found" for the browser library, though it was run from the project folder: an ES module resolves its imports from the script file's own folder, never from the folder it is run in. Two more runs were lost after it to guessed selectors (a button found by a word in its title matched a hidden tab first) before the script was steered by the real element read from the running page.   «step kept»
- **Suggested improvement:** In the walk-scripts guide: a script kept outside the project loads the library with `createRequire(process.cwd() + '/package.json')('playwright')`, run from the project folder; and find a control's selector by reading the running page first (its id at the point pressed), never by a word that may also sit in a hidden control's title.   «step kept»
- **Principle:** Module lookup follows the file, not the shell; and a selector guessed from a word is checked against the live page before a script relies on it.   «step kept»

- **Suggested improvement:** In the skill's merge step: when the handoff file clashes, resolve by keeping both blocks whole, then count the opening and closing markers (`grep -c '<!-- now:'` must equal `grep -c '<!-- /now -->'`) before staging — or rebuild the region from each side's own block (`git show :2:HANDOFF.md`, `:3:`) instead of deleting conflict marks.   «step kept»
- **Principle:** When both sides of a conflict end in the same line, git keeps that line once, outside the conflict; "keep both" then needs that line added back to the first side — count paired markers after any such resolution.   «step kept»

+ **Date:** 8 Nov 26   «chat kept»
+ **Session context:** chat 16, [LW-PIN-LAST-FRAME] (D1870) — re-measuring a pinned row after a CSS scroll-timeline change (numbered past 883, held on another branch)   «chat kept»
+ **Skill:** New skill candidate: measuring-scroll-performance   «chat kept»
+ **Type:** open-source   «chat kept»
+ **Phase/Area:** the before/after frame measure   «chat kept»
+    «chat kept»
+ **Issue:** The measure counted frames "over 33.4 ms" — the exact edge of two screen refreshes — so a frame landing a tenth of a millisecond either side flipped the count, and the before/after medians looked like noise (4 → 17). Pooling every run's raw intervals into buckets (under 20, one refresh skipped, 34.5–50, over 50) showed a fivefold rise in skipped refreshes; a second run with only the suspect style switched off (injected CSS) showed the cost was that one rule, and three cheaper variants were ruled out in minutes. One run's "the page works a third less" did not repeat.   «chat kept»
+    «chat kept»
+ **Suggested improvement:** A frame measure records every raw interval, reports buckets around each refresh multiple rather than one threshold count, repeats the run before believing a total, and diagnoses by switching the suspect rule off for one run before any fix is written.   «chat kept»
+    «chat kept»
+ **Principle:** A threshold placed on a quantised value measures rounding; bucket around the quanta, repeat the run, and isolate a suspected cause by removing it alone.   «chat kept»
+    «chat kept»
